description: EXPERIMENTAL: ANS is a draft standard and Porkbun's registry is new, so behaviour, fields and records may change; tell the user before they depend on it. PUBLIC AND PERMANENT: a registered agent is listed in the public directory and sealed in the transparency log; there is no unlisted option and revoking does not erase the record, so tell the user and don't register agents they want kept private. Give an AI agent a verifiable name with the Agent Name Service (free): `ans://v1.0.0.<host>`, an identity certificate, DNS discovery records, a public entry in Porkbun's transparency log, and a listing in the agent directory. Needs: (0) the agent host to be a domain registered at Porkbun in this account, or a subdomain of one (ANS_DOMAIN_NOT_ELIGIBLE otherwise; external domains added to the account don't count); (1) the agent already serving HTTPS at `endpoint_url` with a publicly trusted certificate (Let's Encrypt is fine); its served chain is registered; (2) `identity_csr_pem`, a certificate request the USER makes on their own machine so the private key never leaves them: `openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out identity.key` then `openssl req -new -key identity.key -out identity.csr -subj "/CN=<host>" -addext "subjectAltName=DNS:<host>,URI:ans://v<version>.<host>"` (P-256 is the curve ES256 signing needs; RSA 2048+ and P-384 also work, but Ed25519, P-521 and EC keys with EXPLICIT curve parameters are refused — the one-step `-newkey ec -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve` form produces the explicit kind on macOS, which is why this is two commands) (the version in the URI must match `version`). Never generate or ask for the private key yourself. Returns agentId and `agentStatus: PENDING_VALIDATION` (`status` is the SUCCESS/ERROR envelope), with `dnsResults` (records published for you when the domain is on Porkbun nameservers in this account; any with published=false must be added at the user's DNS host). Then call advance_ans_agent until `agentStatus` is ACTIVE. Fill `capabilities` with what the agent really does: it is what people search the directory by. Errors: ANS_SERVER_CERT_UNREACHABLE (endpoint not serving HTTPS yet), ANS_SERVER_CERT_INVALID, ANS_ALREADY_REGISTERED (register a higher version).

agent_host.description: Override the host taken from endpoint_url. The user must control its DNS.

capabilities.description: What the agent can do, e.g. [{name:"domain_search", tags:["domains","search"]}].

display_name.description: Shown in the directory. Defaults to the host.

dry_run.description: Check the request without registering anything or writing DNS.

endpoint_url.description: The https:// URL the agent listens on, e.g. https://myagent.example.com/mcp. Its host is the agent host.

identity_csr_pem.description: PEM CSR for the agent identity, made by the user (see description).

metadata_url.description: Capability card URL, if the agent has one.

protocol.description: Guessed from the path when omitted (/mcp -> MCP, agent-card.json or /a2a -> A2A).

server_certificate_pem.description: Full chain (leaf first). Usually omit: the chain the endpoint serves is used.

version.description: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, default 1.0.0. Must match the version in the CSR's ans:// URI.
